entry.title: Social Summary: November 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Governance shock dominated the day: Casey Newton amplified a WSJ report that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang — the batch's highest-scored and most consequential story, though still unconfirmed.

  • AI-for-science had a strong day: Demis Hassabis announced AlphaGenome 2 for predicting DNA variant effects across cell types, and DeepMind claimed the first code-level formal security proof of Signal's protocol.
  • Google launched Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/1M tokens, with Artificial Analysis independently reporting a leading 66 score on its Decision Index v2.1.
  • Open robotics momentum: Runway released Praxis-1 under Apache 2.0, while Jim Fan demoed GR00T 2 autonomously running a chemistry-lab experiment.
  • Ethan Mollick argued coding's AI transformation is far ahead of public perception; Matt Shumer shared a 400B-token Claude Fable 5.2 guide, and the Perplexity CEO showed a Teammate agent building a game autonomously.
  • Perplexity published red-teaming findings on its open-source SPACE sandbox; former White House advisor Ben Buchanan argued China could lead in AI absent chip export controls.
  • Ecosystem funding: UK chip startup Fractile raised $720M at a ~$7B valuation; n8n shipped an open-source personal agent claiming 98% task completion.
entry.content:
Governance shock dominated the day: Casey Newton amplified a WSJ report that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang — the batch's highest-scored and most consequential story, though still unconfirmed.

  • AI-for-science had a strong day: Demis Hassabis announced AlphaGenome 2 for predicting DNA variant effects across cell types, and DeepMind claimed the first code-level formal security proof of Signal's protocol.
  • Google launched Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/1M tokens, with Artificial Analysis independently reporting a leading 66 score on its Decision Index v2.1.
  • Open robotics momentum: Runway released Praxis-1 under Apache 2.0, while Jim Fan demoed GR00T 2 autonomously running a chemistry-lab experiment.
  • Ethan Mollick argued coding's AI transformation is far ahead of public perception; Matt Shumer shared a 400B-token Claude Fable 5.2 guide, and the Perplexity CEO showed a Teammate agent building a game autonomously.
  • Perplexity published red-teaming findings on its open-source SPACE sandbox; former White House advisor Ben Buchanan argued China could lead in AI absent chip export controls.
  • Ecosystem funding: UK chip startup Fractile raised $720M at a ~$7B valuation; n8n shipped an open-source personal agent claiming 98% task completion.

entry.title: Wow: the @WSJ says Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang https://t.co/jgYCHCzWrb
entry.summary: Casey Newton amplifies a Wall Street Journal report claiming Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, a potentially seismic governance story for the company at the center of the AI hardware boom.

entry.title: Super proud to announce AlphaGenome 2 - our new DNA sequence model! 🧬 It predicts the impact of DNA ...
entry.summary: Demis Hassabis announces AlphaGenome 2, a DNA sequence model that predicts the impact of DNA variants across specific cell types for understanding complex diseases, available to academic researchers via API.

entry.title:
Introducing Gemini Decision 1, our new frontier decision model in the Gemini API.
It is $0.10 per ...
entry.summary: A Google-affiliated product lead announces Gemini Decision 1, described as a new frontier decision model available in the Gemini API at $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with native support for image, audio, video and PDF inputs, a 256K context window, and 1K questions, with free API access to try.

entry.title: Today, we’re making Praxis-1 available to everyone. Our state-of-the-art world action model turns vi...
entry.summary: RunwayML announces the open release of Praxis-1, a state-of-the-art world action model that converts video pretraining into real-robot control, shipping with open weights under Apache 2.0 for running and fine-tuning on own hardware.

entry.title: People who have no contact with coders seem to have no idea how much an entire profession transforme...
entry.summary: Mollick argues that people without contact with programmers underestimate how much the coding profession transformed in under a year due to AI, pushing back against claims that AI changed nothing, that AI code is poor, or that companies are retreating from AI.

entry.title: Autonomous, uncut, 1x speed. This is GR00T 2 controlling real dexterous hands to perform a chemistry...
entry.summary: Jim Fan shares a video of GR00T 2 autonomously controlling real dexterous robot hands to run a chemistry lab experiment end to end and clean up afterwards, promising a series of unedited, real-time robot videos without speed-up labels.

entry.title: For the first time, AI has mathematically proven @signalapp’s protocol is secure down to the code le...
entry.summary: DeepMind claims a first: AI has mathematically proven Signal's messaging protocol secure down to the code level, using the AlphaProof Code framework to verify the cryptography protecting billions of messages.

entry.title: Google has released its first decision model, Gemini Decision 1, scoring 66 on the Artificial Analys...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports on Google's first decision model, Gemini Decision 1, which scores 66 on their Decision Index v2.1 — leading knowledge and reasoning benchmarks but trailing leaders Drex Max v1.1 and GLiDE v1.2 (both at 73). The post details pricing ($0.10/1M input tokens, $345 per 1M Tasks, roughly 3x the cost of Drex Max v1.1) and notes weaknesses on a proprietary classification/extraction benchmark.

entry.title: Great performance improvements for attention with almost no downside: matching the FP32 baseline usi...
entry.summary: Istoica promotes a new research result showing attention mechanisms can match an FP32 baseline using 8-bit or even 4-bit quantization, claiming large performance gains with almost no downside.

entry.title: The counterexample to AI diffusion taking a long time is coding, where the complete transformation o...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that coding is the counterexample to slow AI diffusion: professional transformation via coding agents is well underway less than a year after their arrival, faster than historical technology adoption in professions.

entry.title:
Anyhow, in a little over a week we will see the release of The Last Human Game.
There will never be...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick predicts that GTA 6 will be the last AAA game made at scale without AI assistance, arguing future generations will view an all-human billion-dollar game the way we view the Pyramids.

entry.title: Your heart, brain, and immune system share the same DNA sequence. So how can a single-letter change ...
entry.summary: DeepMind's thread-opening post introduces AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that zooms in on specific cell types to help scientists understand what drives disease despite shared DNA across tissues. This is the most engaged post of the thread by far.

entry.title: Meet Déjà View, a model that turns photos taken from different angles into 3D geometry and camera po...
entry.summary: NVIDIA AI introduces Déjà View, a 117M-parameter research model that reconstructs 3D geometry and camera positions from photos taken at different angles by looping a single transformer block, matching or outperforming models up to 10x larger across five benchmarks; presented as a NeurIPS 2026 oral paper with code released.

entry.title:
New research on red teaming our sandbox platform SPACE:
1. CTF red-teaming should prompt explicitl...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas shares new research on red-teaming Perplexity's open-source sandbox platform SPACE, reporting five findings: CTF red-teaming requires explicit prompting to break host-guest isolation; non-cyber models (e.g., GPT-5.6 Sol) outperformed cyber-specialized variants (GPT-5.6 Sol Cyber) at finding exploits; the platform withstood sandbox isolation exploits; a DNS spoofing network bypass was discovered and fixed; and findings are being shared openly with the agent sandbox and security community.

entry.title: Had a Teammate run on Fable 5.2 for a few hours and build an endless zombie shooter that you can pla...
entry.summary: The Perplexity CEO reports having a Perplexity Teammate run for a few hours on Anthropic's Fable 5.2 model to autonomously build a playable browser-based endless zombie shooter with no 3D assets, all generated purely in code, sharing the playable link.

entry.title: Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen says China could already be ahead of the US in AI if Wash...
entry.summary: Former White House AI advisor Ben Buchanan argues China could be ahead of or much closer to the US in AI absent chip export restrictions, stating China lacks only computing power, not talent, money, or electricity, citing DeepSeek papers and Chinese AI CEOs, and criticizing the Trump administration for repealing and under-enforcing export controls, calling China's current closeness a policy choice.

entry.title: This is not an argument that AI is all good or a hype post that you should learn AI today or fall be...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick clarifies that his prior remarks were neither AI hype nor doom: he argues there is a limited window to shape the AI transition so professions improve while remaining human-centered, and that ignoring reality will not achieve that.

entry.title:
End of an era.
Was just watching the video that I shot of Jensen at GTC this spring. He was on top...
entry.summary: Scoble posts a lengthy reflection claiming WSJ and NYT report NVIDIA's board is meeting to fire Jensen Huang amid a personal-conduct scandal, arguing this is a huge loss for NVIDIA despite its strong leadership bench, and warning investors will be affected.

entry.title: Even I, who has been talking about AI for a long time, has been surprised at how fast things have al...
entry.summary: Mollick notes that even as a long-time AI commentator he has been surprised by how quickly AI has fundamentally altered a major profession, observing that adoption and transformation usually take much longer, and predicting coding will not be the only field affected.

entry.title:
The anti-AI backlash in games is mostly hurting indie studios.
Insisting on no AI code in a world w...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues the anti-AI backlash in gaming mostly harms indie studios, calling a no-AI-code standard impossible when all coding will involve AI, and suggesting fans reward human-centered games rather than police AI use.

entry.title:
I burned 400B+ tokens learning to use Fable 5.2.
I packed every single trick I learned into one 17-...
entry.summary: Matt Shumer says he burned over 400 billion tokens learning to use Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and condensed his lessons into a 17-minute video of prompt engineering and agentic-coding techniques.

entry.title: Hey, remember “talk to your documents” RAG-based solutions as the future of AI? Crazy times a year a...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reflects on how RAG-based 'talk to your documents' solutions were seen as the future of AI only about a year and a half ago, remarking on how quickly the field has moved.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: UK chip startup Fractile just raised $720M, and its valuation jumped from about...
entry.summary: Explainer on UK AI chip startup Fractile's $720M raise, lifting its valuation from roughly $1B to $7B in six months. Details include founder Walter Goodwin's Oxford robotics background, a memory-on-processor chip architecture replacing high-bandwidth memory, an approximately $250M Anthropic chip deal for 2027 hardware, and investors including Accel, Conviction, Felicis, Balderton, and T. Rowe Price.

entry.title: Take away its tools, and Claude Fable 5.2 scores below Claude Haiku 5.5 with tools on VIALS-AA; acro...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis presents VIALS-AA results: tool use roughly doubles average scores (~25% to ~47%); Claude Fable 5.2 (max) leads at 67% with tools ($4.20/task) but scores 44% without ($0.73), while Claude Haiku 5.5 with tools scores 49% at $0.07 per task, beating Fable without tools at a tenth of the cost.

entry.title: This is nuts. I just checked in on my agents, and they've pushed five new versions of the game, fixi...
entry.summary: Matt Shumer reports that his autonomous AI agents pushed five new versions of a game overnight, fixing all user-reported issues, describing the game as effectively self-improving and asking players to keep submitting bug reports.

entry.title:
n8n just released a personal agent.
Open source!
Seems pretty awesome: 98% task completion using G...
entry.summary: Svpino announces n8n's release of an open source personal agent, citing 98% task completion when using GPT-6.1 Sol in October benchmarks, and praises n8n's fast-iterating Labs division.

entry.title: Former White House AI advisor @BuchananBen admits the Biden administration should have moved 30-50% ...
entry.summary: Former White House AI advisor Ben Buchanan admits the Biden administration should have moved 30-50% more aggressively on AI chip controls, noting the gap between the 2021 memo and October 2022 implementation, failure to anticipate test-time compute raising memory chip importance, and unaddressed chip smuggling.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Runway just released Praxis-1 with open weights, a robot model trained mostly o...
entry.summary: Explainer thread on Runway's open-weights robotics model Praxis-1, which is pretrained largely on ordinary web video rather than robot demonstration data. The post cites benchmark comparisons (16.1 cm vs 16.0 cm placement error vs robot-footage pretraining), cross-domain generalization from studio to home kitchen, and claimed wins over FLUX 3 Action, Cosmos 3 Nano, and pi0.5.

entry.title: By predicting how the same DNA is read differently from cell to cell, AlphaGenome 2 opens up entirel...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2's availability for non-commercial research via API and Colab tutorials, highlighting its ability to predict how identical DNA is read differently across cell types.

entry.title: We are publishing new research on our findings from red-teaming SPACE, our VM sandbox for Computer a...
entry.summary: Perplexity announces new research red-teaming SPACE, its VM sandbox for computer-use agents: 12 models were given tasks to escape the VM for a host credential and bypass network policy to reach a blocked URL; key findings are that standard CTF setups can steer agents away from the tested boundary and security-specialized models do not guarantee better results.

entry.title: NVIDIA used our MolmoSpaces benchmark to evaluate GR00T 2, alongside RoboCasa365, RoboLab, & Rob...
entry.summary: The Allen Institute for AI (@allen_ai) notes that NVIDIA used AI2's open MolmoSpaces benchmark to evaluate its GR00T 2 robotics model alongside other robotics benchmarks like RoboCasa365, RoboLab, and RoboDojo, and invites other teams to test robot policies on the same simulated environments.

entry.title: Runway CEO @agermanidis reveals that Praxis-1 can adapt to a humanoid robot using less than 30 minut...

entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas explains that the name Perplexity Computer was inspired by Dylan Patel's (SemiAnalysis) blog post framing coding agents as a new kind of computer, expressing pleasure that the framing proved useful to Patel and SemiAnalysis.

entry.title:

entry.summary: IBM GM Shaun Clowes argues that coding tools like Claude Code remain copilots limited by human speed, and that the real breakthrough will be fully autonomous business functions operating without human oversight, which he says is only at its very beginning.

entry.title:

entry.summary: LlamaIndex founder Jerry Liu lays out the company's strategic repositioning as an applied research lab for document OCR and document work, detailing five investment pillars: benchmarks (ParseBench, ExtractBench, ExtractBench Pro), data curation and synthetic data, compute/training (producing the OCRia-1 model), agent optimization at the accuracy/cost/latency pareto frontier, and feedback loops.

entry.title: 📢 New issue brief: In 2025, 56 federal agencies reported 3,611 AI use cases. How do they know these ...
entry.summary: Stanford HAI announces a new issue brief, produced with Stanford RegLab, examining how the 56 federal agencies reporting 3,611 AI use cases in 2025 can verify whether those tools actually work, and presenting a blueprint for evaluating AI in public services.

entry.title: Tools matter most for counting tasks, which need an exact tally of many small objects. With tools, m...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis explains that tools matter most for counting tasks in VIALS-AA: Fable drops from 65% to 9% without tools, Opus 5.5 from 57% to 4%, and Sonnet 5.5 from 65% to 13%, while GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol hold up better (61%/35% and 61%/39%), and some domains like phylogenetics are less tool-dependent.

entry.title:

entry.summary: The vLLM project announces day-0 support for Runway's Praxis-1 in vLLM-Omni: a video-pretrained model for robot control with Apache 2.0 open weights and cross-embodiment adaptation. The integration takes camera observations, robot state, and task instructions to generate action chunks, supporting offline inference and OpenPI/Positronic serving, qualified on a single H100 80GB.

entry.title:
vLLM EPD, now upgraded 🚀
DeepInfer demonstrated the value of EPD disaggregation. vLLM’s latest EPD ...
entry.summary: vLLM announces upgraded EPD (encode-prefill-decode) disaggregation delivering lower TTFT and higher per-GPU throughput, integrated with vLLM Router, SMG, and llm-d; the thread's lead post with the strongest engagement of the series.

entry.summary: Rox CEO Ishan Mukherjee argues enterprise AI-agent sales pitches based on hours saved are dead after three years of Copilot and Agentforce underdelivering; buyers now want coding agents that ship code and revenue agents that drive revenue.

entry.summary: RunwayML argues general video is the most scalable robotics data source; fine-tuned on RT-1, an unseen embodiment, Praxis-1 reportedly reaches 80.0% on SimplerEnv versus 52.4% for the original RT-1 policy.

entry.title:

The more code you write, the more complex it is to keep ...
entry.summary: Svpino highlights a core problem with agentic coding: as AI-generated code accumulates, teams must handle measurement, staged rollouts, and rollback strategies for every new feature to avoid production failures, teasing a solution in a follow-up.

entry.title: Tools raise the cost per task for every model, but by very different amounts. Astra costs $0.27 per ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis analyzes how tools raise per-task cost differently across models: Astra $0.27 vs $0.21, Sol $0.06 vs $0.05, Fable $4.20 vs $0.73 (5.8x), with the largest multiples for Qwen3.8 Max (0902) at 28x, Gemini 3.8 Flash at 20x, and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at 15x; smaller models with tools are often the cheapest route to a given score.

entry.summary: NVIDIA announces an expanded partnership with ElevenLabs to bring voice agents to enterprises and governments, with NVIDIA Nemotron models now available in ElevenAgents for building customizable voice agents.

entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports Google DeepMind's release of AlphaGenome 2, an upgraded model predicting DNA mutation effects in specific cell types, highlighting cell-type zooming versus tissue blending, nearly double the regulatory mutation detection, and generalization to unseen cell types from small lab samples.

entry.title:

Testing via a custom Mac app on Image Playground shows it is strongest at editing and swapping elements in photos, weaker at clean-ups and reframing, and weakest at generating images from scratch. Apple refused 8% of prompts; no API exists so they built their own harness.

entry.summary: Thread opener from Artificial Analysis: they benchmarked Apple's ADM 3 Cloud photo-editing model through their arena, finding it ranks #42 on AA-Image-Editing v2.1 and #85 on AA-Image-T2I v2.1.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 11, 2026
entry.summary:
The community's attention split between landmark commercialization news and escalating safety anxiety. Anthropic's IPO roadshow launch was the day's defining financial event, reinforced by an unusual goodwill usage reset for Claude subscribers. OpenAI's beta of Businesses in ChatGPT signaled the start of chatbot-native commerce, drawing massive engagement.

  • Jim Fan unveiled NVIDIA GR00T 2, an open robotics foundation model running onboard, while Google DeepMind shipped Gemini Robotics 2.5 — physical AI was a dominant theme
  • Safety discourse intensified: Paul Christiano's coin-flip takeover warning, the Forecast Research Institute's recursive self-improvement report, and Factory's Varun Nair flagging agentic offensive-security risk from open-weight models
  • Artificial Analysis partnered with DeepMind on the MKA agentic-vision benchmark; Nathan Lambert argued human expertise underpins AI diffusion; Hugging Face crossed 20M builders
  • Gary Marcus amplified the Jensen Huang political controversy, earning huge engagement but a polarized reception
entry.content:
The community's attention split between landmark commercialization news and escalating safety anxiety. Anthropic's IPO roadshow launch was the day's defining financial event, reinforced by an unusual goodwill usage reset for Claude subscribers. OpenAI's beta of Businesses in ChatGPT signaled the start of chatbot-native commerce, drawing massive engagement.

  • Jim Fan unveiled NVIDIA GR00T 2, an open robotics foundation model running onboard, while Google DeepMind shipped Gemini Robotics 2.5 — physical AI was a dominant theme
  • Safety discourse intensified: Paul Christiano's coin-flip takeover warning, the Forecast Research Institute's recursive self-improvement report, and Factory's Varun Nair flagging agentic offensive-security risk from open-weight models
  • Artificial Analysis partnered with DeepMind on the MKA agentic-vision benchmark; Nathan Lambert argued human expertise underpins AI diffusion; Hugging Face crossed 20M builders
  • Gary Marcus amplified the Jensen Huang political controversy, earning huge engagement but a polarized reception

entry.title: Anthropic has launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering: https://t.co/FhVRVuWN9...
entry.summary: Anthropic officially announces it has launched the roadshow for its proposed IPO, with the standard SEC legal disclaimers about the registration statement.

entry.title:
Now in beta: Businesses in ChatGPT.
Claim your business, manage your information, and get insights ...
entry.summary: OpenAI launches Businesses in ChatGPT in beta: a hub where companies can claim their business, manage their information, get engagement insights, and build Business Agents to answer customer questions.

entry.title: Introducing GR00T 2: our most advanced, open System One model for robotics. It runs entirely on your...
entry.summary: Jim Fan introduces GR00T 2, NVIDIA's most advanced open robotics foundation model, running fully on onboard robot compute, with long-horizon dexterous tasks (20+ steps, 5+ minutes), X-Adapt for zero-shot sim/wearable-to-robot transfer, unified cognition via frontier-agent integration, and an open release including weights, 100K hours of training data, simulation and annotation engines, and hardware designs.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: OpenAI board member Paul Christiano says that if we continue to build AI as quic...
entry.summary: Reports that OpenAI board member Paul Christiano stated the risk of an AI takeover within the next 3 years is a coin flip if AI development continues at maximum speed. A high-profile existential risk statement from someone with direct governance access at a leading AI lab.

entry.title:
Gemini Robotics 2.5 is here. 🤖
Our latest physical AI is able to learn hundreds of everyday skills ...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5, its latest physical AI model capable of learning hundreds of everyday skills from folding laundry to autonomously sorting car parts on factory floors, with a capabilities thread.

entry.title: We’ve partnered with Google DeepMind to launch their Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) evaluation, a ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a partnership with Google DeepMind to launch the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark: 200 private real-world visual tasks across 10 industries where agents work from dense visual files like schematics and scans to produce deliverables such as slide decks, spreadsheets and marked-up images, with Climb vs Regression rubric scoring.

entry.title: 🚨MAJOR BREAKING NEWS: President Trump lied on Monday about when he had been told that Jensen Huang w...
entry.summary: Marcus shares breaking-news style claims that President Trump lied about when he learned Jensen Huang was in a relationship with a Chinese spy allegedly receiving chips, asserting Trump knew since May and ignored warnings from Rubio despite national security risks.

entry.title: Had early access to Gemini 4 Carbon, it is a very good model that improves on Argon. It is useful to...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reviews early access to Gemini 4 Carbon, calling it a strong improvement over Argon with strengths and weaknesses distinct from Claude/GPT, and demos it reproducing a video clip in Three.js.

entry.title: We've given all Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team users one free full reset, across all models and limits. U...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude developer account announces a free full usage reset for Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team subscribers (usable before December 10), compensating for recently fixed bugs that consumed more usage limits than intended, noting earlier Fable resets were insufficient for users already at weekly caps.

entry.title: @simonsarris we will have more models soon which are more widely accessible, the reality is that Car...
entry.summary: A Google AI executive responds to a user, explaining that the Gemini-4 Carbon and Argon models are expensive to run and therefore not scalable for wide release, while promising more broadly accessible frontier models in the near future.

entry.title: It could be vastly underestimated how much human expertise is needed to diffuse the benefits of AI t...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues the AI industry underestimates how much human expertise is needed to diffuse AI benefits across long-tail knowledge work, suggesting data companies like Mercor brand experts as partners who improve tools rather than be replaced, and noting knowledge work is more interpersonal and context-driven than evals suggest.

entry.title: We just crossed: - 20M AI builders on @huggingface - 300PB of models, datasets, agent traces, and R...
entry.summary: Clement Delangue announces Hugging Face crossed 20M AI builders and 300PB of hosted models, datasets, agent traces, and RL environments (9PB added in one week), with October its biggest month for DAUs, MAUs, and revenue.

entry.title:
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is here, bringing adaptive AI reasoning in real-time to the vehicle. 🚘
From ...
entry.summary: NVIDIA announces Alpamayo 2 Edge, bringing real-time adaptive AI reasoning to vehicles: it plans driving paths and explains decisions, from yielding to pedestrians to making room for oncoming buses. Developers can build on the open model to create autonomous vehicles adapted to their own fleets.

entry.title:
AI companies increasingly say they may soon reach recursive self-improvement (RSI).
With RSI, AI ca...
entry.summary: Thread lead from the Forecast Research Institute introducing a new report on how close AI is to recursive self-improvement: the report reviews evidence, turns key disagreements into forecasting questions, and gives initial LLM forecasts, warning acceleration could occur inside AI companies before outsiders notice.

entry.title:
The Huang Affair is the new Watergate.
It no longer just about Jensen or Nvidia. It’s about what th...
entry.summary: Marcus frames the Jensen Huang controversy as a Watergate-style scandal, arguing the core question is what the US government knew and when.

entry.title: Claude now supports more of the MCP Apps extension, such as app tools and embedded sites, so your fu...
entry.summary: Anthropic's headline post announcing that Claude now supports more of the MCP Apps extension — app tools and embedded sites — so developers' full applications can run inside Claude, with a link to start building.

entry.title: MKA tests models’ visual understanding of documents including engineering schematics, architectural ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis describes its MKA benchmark testing model visual understanding of documents like engineering schematics, architectural drawings, and clinical scans, with deliverables like slide decks and marked-up images. Example: Claude Fable 5.2 (max) took 224 turns including 203 image views, costing ~$68 for one building-plan audit task.

entry.title:
This is a pretty cool idea:
Let your agent simulate each potential action before picking the best o...
entry.summary: svpino explains IFM's PAN 2 world model, which uses simulative reasoning: an agent simulates candidate actions before acting, as illustrated by a surfer testing three moments to pop up on a wave. Technical breakdown of Generative Latent Prediction: an LLM handles conceptual reasoning while a 29B latent diffusion model handles perceptual rendering, with weights and code released under Apache 2.0.

entry.title: AI hacking capabilities that were restricted by frontier model guardrails just months ago are now av...
entry.summary: Factory's Varun Nair warns that open-weight models now match frontier models on offensive security capabilities, and that custom attack harnesses like ARTEX and HexStrike are already used in real attacks. He says the Mythos model alarmed CISOs and that an October wave of AI-driven breaches, dubbed Black October, forced security budget reassessments.

entry.title:
We have another open-weight model, and this one is a beast!
Model: Tencent Hy4.
You can use the mo...
entry.summary: An AI educator highlights Tencent's Hy4 open-weight model, noting it is usable now with weights to follow in weeks, supports vision and computer use, and competes with Kimi K3.1 Pro; he cites the preview version's 780B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts architecture.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Mercor just raised $750M at a $20B valuation, and says it grew from $1M to $3B ...
entry.summary: MTS explains Mercor's $750M raise at a $20B valuation, doubling from its October 2025 Series C, with $614M first-half 2026 revenue, a $2B run rate by June, over 5 million paid experts training frontier models, NVIDIA using Mercor data for its two latest Nemotron models, and inference spend at 3x salaries. Includes a quote from Sophia Dew on AI agents and task bundles.

entry.title:
Start building with Gemini 4 Carbon: our strongest model for complex, long-horizon tasks.
It’s desi...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's headline post inviting developers to build with Gemini 4 Carbon, described as its strongest model for complex, long-horizon tasks with extended verification loops across software engineering, cybersecurity, knowledge work, and science.

entry.title: Keenable Search 1.0 takes 1st (pro, 83) and 2nd (realtime, 82) on the Artificial Analysis Search Ind...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Keenable Search 1.0 ranks 1st (pro, 83) and 2nd (realtime, 82) on its Search Index, ahead of Exa and Perplexity at 80; scores jumped from 67 in August, ~50 points above the same model without search. Benchmarked over 1700 tasks at ~$0.040/task, over a third below the median, and among the fastest products measured.

entry.title: AI capability progress has not clearly accelerated on public measures. That said, there is some inte...
entry.summary: FRI reports that public measures show no clear capability acceleration, but internal evidence hints otherwise: METR's preliminary assessment in the Claude Opus 5.5 system card estimated ~1.5X acceleration inside Anthropic (30% chance of 2X), OpenAI experiments per experimenter hit an all-time high in Aug 2026, and a post-cutoff METR report estimates Anthropic progress is now ~2X earlier rates with ~80% AI-attributed.

entry.title: With @ArtificialAnlys, we built MKA (Multimodal Knowledge Agent): a benchmark for how well agents ha...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind, with Artificial Analysis, introduces MKA, a benchmark measuring how well agents handle visually complex professional tasks like cross-referencing blueprints and reading scientific charts, claiming Gemini 4 Carbon ranks second at 6x lower average cost per task than the top model.

entry.title:
Use Business Hub to shape what customers see about your business in ChatGPT.
Once verified, you can...
entry.summary: OpenAI details Business Hub, letting verified businesses manage their ChatGPT presence, create Business Agents, add product feeds with pricing and availability, and view aggregated insights on mentions and clicks, while stating user conversations are not shared with businesses.

entry.title:
With RSI, current AI systems help develop future AI systems.
AI companies now say this loop has beg...
entry.summary: FRI reports AI companies claim the RSI loop has begun: Anthropic's IPO filing update claims it now meets its definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI, and OpenAI says it achieved an automated AI research intern in Sep 2026 and targets an automated AI researcher by Mar 2028.

entry.title: This model has frontier level cyber capabilities and so the team has been hard at work making sure i...
entry.summary: Logan K explains the team worked hard on safety preparations before broadly deploying a model with frontier-level cyber capabilities, thanking users for patience and promising continued shipping.

entry.title: Factory's @varinnair warns most companies are still defending against human hackers, while AI agents...
entry.summary: Factory's Varun Nair warns that security practices are still designed around human attackers while AI agents now execute hundreds to thousands of operations per hour, run intrusions end-to-end autonomously, and probe multiple infrastructure components in parallel.

entry.title: Looks like Fable 5.2 is above the already steep trendline on three of the most informative unsaturat...
entry.summary: Mollick observes that Claude Fable 5.2 sits above the trendline on three informative unsaturated benchmarks: ECI (a composite), Remote Labor (end-to-end freelance job performance), and RoboDojo (robot control).

entry.title:
You can also publish a Business Agent to help people explore what you offer.
Customers can ask ques...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces Business Agents, branded agents in ChatGPT that let customers ask questions and compare products, clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT's independent answers, available to eligible US ecommerce and service businesses.

entry.title: claim your business on ChatGPT and engage with customers in new ways:
entry.summary: Greg Brockman announces/promotes that businesses can claim their listing on ChatGPT to engage with customers.

entry.title: HUGE news. One side Goldman is flogging Anthropic’s IPO while the other is taking away their tools f...
entry.summary: Marcus highlights an apparent contradiction: Goldman Sachs is underwriting or promoting Anthropic's IPO while simultaneously restricting the use of Anthropic's tools for many of its own employees.

entry.title:
Huge AI announcements from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Google in the past 48 hours.
Here's everyth...
entry.summary: Rowan Cheung summarizes a burst of AI news: AI 2027 authors moving timelines up to 2027, Anthropic's IPO pitch opening, OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT launch, and Anthropic's Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Claude Data updates.

entry.title: NEW: Anthropic is rolling out a wave of work tools inside Claude, including Whiteboards, Sheets, Mee...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports Anthropic is launching productivity tools inside Claude: Meetings (joining Google Meet calls with follow-up work), Sheets (building spreadsheets from descriptions), Whiteboards (organizing brainstorms into boards convertible to slides/docs), Data dashboards out of beta, and connectors for Adobe, Atlassian and Box.

entry.title: 🎉 Great work from the PAN 2 team on an open-weight world model built for real-world simulation, grou...
entry.summary: vLLM project congratulates the PAN 2 team on an open-weight world model grounded in time, physics, and space for real-world simulation, announcing Day-0 vLLM-Omni support for PAN 2 text-to-video and image-to-video generation through an open inference stack.

entry.title:
We turned these cruxes into 18 forecasting questions.
To measure acceleration, we propose a forecas...
entry.summary: FRI describes converting debate cruxes into 18 forecasting questions, defining a fast year as a 30+ point rise in the Epoch Capabilities Index; an ensemble of four frontier LLMs gives ~40% odds of a fast year by 2030 (ranging from 35% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 to ~56% for GPT-6 Astra), with ~70% attribution to AI automation of R&D if it occurs.

entry.title:
Of course, AI companies are not necessarily neutral observers. So how close is RSI really?
In the r...
entry.summary: FRI notes AI companies are not neutral observers and reviews evidence up to Nov 3, 2026: AI acts as a capable research assistant while humans retain research judgment; no measured Anthropic R&D is fully autonomous, while OpenAI's AI completed 57% of 2-4 hour tasks autonomously in Jul 2026 (up from 28% in Jan) and 35% of 8-16 hour tasks (up from 10%).

entry.title:
I think SWE jobs will be safe from AI, but not the way you think:
2030 prediction:
- AI can write ...
entry.summary: A contrarian 2030 prediction arguing SWE jobs may survive not because AI coding fails, but because token costs will rise: AI will write code better than 99% of humans, but deploying it at scale will be expensive enough that hiring human teams remains cost-competitive.

entry.title: we need fewer one shot demos and more tools that show how you can collaborate with models to bring y...
entry.summary: The author argues that the AI field needs fewer one-shot demos and more tools demonstrating how people can collaborate with models to realize their own creative visions.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 10, 2026
entry.summary:
Independent evaluations were largely glowing, though reviewers flagged limitations and restrictive behavior.

  • Ethan Mollick's early-access 'Jagged AGI' review and his 25,000-agent 3D world-building experiment—with emergent agent bureaucracy—drove the strongest technical discussion
  • Matt Shumer's 400B-token test thread showcased MIRROR EARTH and a code-only movie, popularizing a new workflow meta: Fable 5.2 plans, Opus 5.5 executes
  • Anthropic paired the launch with Mythos 5.2, claiming 30% speed gains, price cuts, and loyalty-based usage resets; its model-selection guide drew 1.5M views
  • Economics takes resonated widely: Pieter Levels on software being easy to build but hard to monetize, and Francois Chollet endorsing autonomous businesses acquiring distressed SaaS
  • Nathan Lambert provoked debate on why OpenRouter's popular open models remain predominantly Chinese; OpenAI disclosed its Control Room safety infrastructure, while Casey Newton sharply criticized Nvidia's governance
entry.content:
Independent evaluations were largely glowing, though reviewers flagged limitations and restrictive behavior.

  • Ethan Mollick's early-access 'Jagged AGI' review and his 25,000-agent 3D world-building experiment—with emergent agent bureaucracy—drove the strongest technical discussion
  • Matt Shumer's 400B-token test thread showcased MIRROR EARTH and a code-only movie, popularizing a new workflow meta: Fable 5.2 plans, Opus 5.5 executes
  • Anthropic paired the launch with Mythos 5.2, claiming 30% speed gains, price cuts, and loyalty-based usage resets; its model-selection guide drew 1.5M views
  • Economics takes resonated widely: Pieter Levels on software being easy to build but hard to monetize, and Francois Chollet endorsing autonomous businesses acquiring distressed SaaS
  • Nathan Lambert provoked debate on why OpenRouter's popular open models remain predominantly Chinese; OpenAI disclosed its Control Room safety infrastructure, while Casey Newton sharply criticized Nvidia's governance

entry.title: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2, taking the #1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2, which takes #1 on Intelligence Index v5 at 65, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (60) and Opus 5.5 (59), with gains in science, knowledge, and coding. Priced at $8/$40 per 1M tokens (a 20% cut from Fable 5.1), but cost per task of $26.5 at max effort is ~2.6x Opus 5.5 and ~2x Fable 5.1. It sets records including 80% on HLE-Diamond.

entry.title: I had early access to Fable 5.2 for a bit & I think it crosses the line into being a sort of Ja...
entry.summary: Mollick reports early access to Fable 5.2 and argues it crosses into being a sort of Jagged AGI, demonstrating it launching a business, doing academic research, hacking hardware, and building 3D models, illustrating both its limits and powers.

entry.title: Meta's newest model Muse Ember scores 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching Cla...
entry.summary: Detailed Artificial Analysis evaluation of Meta's Muse Ember efficient-tier model line: it scores 36 on the AA Intelligence Index, sits on the intelligence-vs-cost Pareto frontier, and is the cheapest model scoring 36+ at $0.14 per task (nearly 3x cheaper than Claude Haiku 5.5 max at the same score). It also scores 68.1% on AutomationBench-AA, level with the far more expensive Muse Wonder (max), and trails Muse Wonder's index score of 44 by 8 points at about 1/50th the cost.

entry.content:
Discussion split between architecture theory, benchmark rigor, and AI's economic impact. Yann LeCun set the technical tone by clarifying JEPA taxonomy, while Artificial Analysis anchored methodology talk with its Decision Index v2 launch.

  • Yann LeCun explained the P in JEPA means predictive, mapping when joint-embedding architectures need predictors versus generative designs
  • Greg Brockman argued test-time-compute frontier models now drive scientific discovery, echoing Shunyu Yao's claim that AI will soon master biology via autonomous labs
  • Ethan Mollick flagged benchmark-fragility research showing trivial edits, like renaming files, can distort coding leaderboard rankings
  • levelsio retired Infinite Slop TV after 17.8M clip views and showed AI compressing i18n work to minutes; Gary Marcus countered that jobs and productivity barely moved
  • Erik Brynjolfsson published a transformative-AI economics agenda; swyx claimed Cursor is thriving post-acquisition

entry.title: @TimDarcet @gabriberton The P in JEPA stands for predictive. The main distinction is not between JEA...
entry.summary: LeCun continues yesterday's Social thread, adding formal loss formulations and the history of anti-collapse methods. Yann LeCun (@ylecun) responds to a discussion by clarifying the taxonomy of joint-embedding architectures: the P in JEPA stands for predictive, and the fundamental distinction is not between JEA and JEPA but between joint-embedding approaches (predictive or not) and generative architectures. He lays out formal loss formulations: generative models predict y from x with a divergence loss between target and prediction, while JEA encodes both x and y and minimizes representation divergence with an anti-collapse regularizer R, useful when neither view has a privileged direction (e.g., two views of the same scene). He adds historical depth, citing Becker and Hinton's 1989 information-maximization anti-collapse model and noting Schmidhuber's early related work, and notes that whether a predictor is needed depends on the task.

entry.title: AA-Symmetry measures how consistent models are when asked equivalent questions. We take a fixed task...
entry.summary: Description of the AA-Symmetry benchmark: 120 base questions with 440 variations testing answer consistency under reordering, label swaps, and negation. Models from baselabs lead, with Mammoth 27B scoring 96 and selecting the same answer 99% of the time versus 67% for Clef.

entry.title: Decision model costs ranged from $14 per 1M Tasks for Celeris-1.1 Decision to $859 for Clef. Celeris...
entry.summary: Cost analysis of decision models: $14 per 1M tasks for Celeris-1.1 Decision up to $859 for Clef, with Pareto frontier analysis including GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at the high end. Explains how multi-pass billing inflates effective cost, e.g. GLiDE v1.2 at $780 per 1M tasks despite cheap token pricing.

entry.title: @bernhardsson Price on its own says nothing about revenue. In both cases the important variable is d...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet responds to Bo Bernhardsson in a discussion about AI pricing and revenue, arguing that price alone is not informative — demand structure is the key variable. He explains that revenue can rise both when price rises and when it falls because there is a core of price-insensitive demand alongside a large pool of price-sensitive latent demand; higher prices extract more from the former, lower prices unlock the latter.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 08, 2026
entry.summary:
Agentic coding and AI-designed physical products dominated the conversation. Andrej Karpathy demoed TristanTube, a 47K-video app one-shotted with Claude Code, while levelsio's viral AI-furniture thread spawned a broader thesis on personal hardware and new maker markets.

  • Francois Chollet argued data/compute scaling is a multiplier on generalization, not a substitute — intersecting with Yann LeCun's detailed SSL/JEPA taxonomy and Gary Marcus's chart calling Anthropic's growth projections fantasy
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shared breakout Teammate launch metrics (3.7x day-two automation growth) and claimed instant PMF as a chief-of-staff assistant
  • Ethan Mollick was highly prolific: amplifying new Anthropic research that AI could absorb 27–52% of researcher time, arguing human fact-checking of AI output is becoming obsolete, and pitching AI-enabled investigative journalism
  • Jim Fan teased an 'extraordinary' CoRL keynote two days out and vouched that a robot demo was genuinely autonomous at real speed
  • Greg Brockman's cryptic note that security architecture matters more than ever reflected rising security anxiety among frontier-lab leaders
entry.content:
Agentic coding and AI-designed physical products dominated the conversation. Andrej Karpathy demoed TristanTube, a 47K-video app one-shotted with Claude Code, while levelsio's viral AI-furniture thread spawned a broader thesis on personal hardware and new maker markets.

  • Francois Chollet argued data/compute scaling is a multiplier on generalization, not a substitute — intersecting with Yann LeCun's detailed SSL/JEPA taxonomy and Gary Marcus's chart calling Anthropic's growth projections fantasy
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shared breakout Teammate launch metrics (3.7x day-two automation growth) and claimed instant PMF as a chief-of-staff assistant
  • Ethan Mollick was highly prolific: amplifying new Anthropic research that AI could absorb 27–52% of researcher time, arguing human fact-checking of AI output is becoming obsolete, and pitching AI-enabled investigative journalism
  • Jim Fan teased an 'extraordinary' CoRL keynote two days out and vouched that a robot demo was genuinely autonomous at real speed
  • Greg Brockman's cryptic note that security architecture matters more than ever reflected rising security anxiety among frontier-lab leaders

entry.title: Data scaling and compute scaling are *multipliers* for the generalization power of an approach. Tril...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that data and compute scaling are multipliers on an approach's generalization power rather than a substitute for it; massive investment can make low-generalization methods look adequate, but a cleverer approach will scale better. He advises researchers to work on methods that can scale while remembering scaling alone is not the end-all of AI.

entry.title: Earlier this week Tristan published his top YouTube channels: https://t.co/NZ3UCNo6cT Which looked e...
entry.summary: Karpathy showcases TristanTube, a 47K-video YouTube-style viewer built from a curated channel list, stating it was one-shotted with Claude Code in about three minutes.

entry.title: @gabriberton Several comments: 1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun provides a detailed technical taxonomy of self-supervised learning methods: distinguishing reconstruction-based from joint-embedding approaches, explaining that DINO is technically a JEA (a kind of JEPA) differing in anti-collapse criterion and augmentation, situating V-JEPA 2.1 as a corporate-lab effort, and separating research papers like LeJEPA from applied/fine-tuned work.

entry.title: Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each pa...
entry.summary: levelsio's viral post describes using Claude Code to design furniture part by part and produce a bill of materials for ordering cheap parts directly from suppliers, bypassing heavily marked-up furniture brands (citing a $30,000 sofa). He notes Opus 5.5 and other models can operate free 3D tools like Blender and FreeCAD, making self-designed furniture practical, and that a non-designer, non-coder (@theannalux) designed a table from scratch working with Claude Code in the terminal, which he argues is superior to the app.

entry.title: Teammate automation runs grew 3.7x from launch day to day two. This is despite day two being a Frida...
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Perplexity Teammates rollout, Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shares adoption metrics for the newly launched Teammate product, reporting automation runs grew 3.7x from launch day to day two despite it being a Friday, and predicts accelerating productivity gains for high-agency professionals.

entry.title: Some new data from Anthropic looking at the impact of AI on the sciences by field: "With current cap...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights new Anthropic research finding that, with current capabilities and wide adoption, AI could take on 27-52% of researcher time needed to produce a new study, with a median of 38% across fields, linking the source.

entry.title: I think there is way too much concern expressed about verification of AI output in everyday work due...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that excessive concern about verifying AI output for factual errors is outdated: recent models now beat human experts, including PhD specialists, at finding facts and checking claims, so human error-checking is no longer the bottleneck it was.

entry.title: AI could do 1000x more research but the jagged frontier currently runs through the fact that the tas...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick (Wharton professor and prominent AI commentator) argues on Bluesky that AI could dramatically accelerate scientific research — potentially 1000x — but that a key bottleneck remains human judgment: the taste for identifying what constitutes an interesting research story. He draws a parallel to the same bottleneck observed in academic research and hedges with the caveat that this may only hold for now.

entry.title: This can be a golden age of investigative journalism. Analyzing filings, records and public data to ...

entry.title: This can be a golden age of investigative journalism. Analyzing filings, records and public data to ...

Yann LeCun defends the JEPA research program in a reply, noting there has been more time between the 2017 transformer paper and ChatGPT than between the original 2022 JEPA paper and today, urging patience for JEPA-based breakthroughs and pointing to V-JEPA and I-JEPA as progress.

entry.title: Breaking: Green line represents a widespread fantasy, and roughly the rocket that Anthropic would ha...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus shares a chart commenting on Anthropic's business trajectory, arguing that the projected growth line is an unrealistic fantasy that would have been needed for Anthropic to become a sustainable business, and that the actual recent figures (dark bars) have fallen behind the required pace, leading him to conclude the company probably will not achieve it.

entry.title:
I think many people are underestimating basic economics
If something is 5x cheaper to buy and it's ...
entry.summary: levelsio argues people underestimate the economics of personal hardware: custom items 5x cheaper and personalized will win as traditional furniture service collapses amid labor shortages and bankruptcies. He frames a second maker wave enabled by AI making hardware design accessible, and speculates suppliers in China could offer custom assembly and worldwide shipping, noting many brands are effectively dropshippers already.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 07, 2026
entry.summary:
Breakthrough claims and evaluation infrastructure dominated AI discussion today. Google DeepMind revealed AI agents uncovered weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA, while reports claimed a non-public Anthropic model helped prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture.

  • Anthropic announced a novel 'dreaming' memory-consolidation capability for Claude, drawing very strong engagement
  • Artificial Analysis launched the VIALS-AA life-sciences leaderboard and quantified DeepSeek V4.1 Flash inference speedups on GB300 hardware
  • OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench for wet-lab agents and a cross-industry cyber-safety framework with the Frontier Model Forum
  • Nathan Lambert argued inference startups face a strategic squeeze; Gary Marcus claimed Anthropic's valuation fell ~50%, fueling bubble debate
  • Clem Delangue highlighted Hugging Face's robotics open-source growth, while MCP servers appearing in creator apps signaled agent-tool convergence

Sentiment mixed frontier-lab optimism about agentic science and memory capabilities with macro anxiety over valuations and inference-provider economics. Independent evaluators like Artificial Analysis gained prominence as the community's trusted arbiters.

  • Artificial Analysis launched the VIALS-AA life-sciences leaderboard and quantified DeepSeek V4.1 Flash inference speedups on GB300 hardware
  • OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench for wet-lab agents and a cross-industry cyber-safety framework with the Frontier Model Forum
  • Nathan Lambert argued inference startups face a strategic squeeze; Gary Marcus claimed Anthropic's valuation fell ~50%, fueling bubble debate
  • Clem Delangue highlighted Hugging Face's robotics open-source growth, while MCP servers appearing in creator apps signaled agent-tool convergence

Sentiment mixed frontier-lab optimism about agentic science and memory capabilities with macro anxiety over valuations and inference-provider economics. Independent evaluators like Artificial Analysis gained prominence as the community's trusted arbiters.

entry.title: We’re launching VIALS-AA, a leaderboard for Handshake AI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in l...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches VIALS-AA, a leaderboard for Handshake AI's VIALS benchmark testing visual reasoning in life sciences and biotech. The 161 tasks span eight domains involving gel blots, flow cytometry plots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies; models run three times in their open-source Stirrup agent harness with code execution and image tools, graded by GPT-6 Luna, with pass^3 scoring. Gemini 4 Carbon leads at 64%, narrowly ahead of GPT-6 Astra, with the top three within 3 points.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: AI physics research lab Physical Superintelligence used a non-public Anthropic C...

Here is how the streaming inference engine works:
• The encoder produces one audio token every 80ms...
entry.summary: svpino breaks down the streaming inference engine design for real-time speech recognition: an 80ms audio token encoder paired with 160ms decoder chunks (6.25 updates per second). entry.title: Social Summary: November 06, 2026
entry.summary:
Breaking capability and security news dominated discussions. OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security-research model reportedly already defending Linux kernel code, announced alongside a major strategic partnership with JPMorganChase.

  • Thomas Wolf released a free ~70,000-word MoE Training Handbook based on 800k GPU hours of experiments, arguing dense open models are 'basically over'
  • METR estimates Anthropic is improving capabilities at ~2× the historical rate, possibly 3×, igniting recursive self-improvement debate; METR also criticized Anthropic for redacting most of its public assessment
  • Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small jumped 18 points to 31 on the Artificial Analysis index; Tencent's Hy4 scored 35, tying Grok 4.7
  • Perplexity launched Teammates proactive work agents, with ~10,000 already active internally — roughly 20× its human headcount
  • Jim Fan introduced VFlash parallel vision decoding for physical AI, while Soumith Chintala shared unusually transparent training details for a small v2 model
  • Gary Marcus went viral declaring a market 'day of reckoning' amid double-digit AI stock losses, echoing voter backlash against new data centers
  • Evaluation distrust ran as a strong undercurrent: swyx argued independent evaluators must rebuild lab benchmarks, and Hamel Husain urged practitioners to run private evals

Community sentiment split between capability optimism — security agents, MoE scale, real agent adoption — and skepticism over benchmark integrity, lab transparency, and market sustainability.

18 of the 20 best open models today are Mixture-of-Experts. Dense is basically over.
And yet the kn...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf (Hugging Face co-founder) announces the free release of an approximately 70,000-word MoE Training Handbook based on 800k GPU hours of their own experiments, covering expert sizing, all-to-all communication overhead, router choices in fp32, auxiliary loss vs loss-free bias, upcycling dense checkpoints, and serving with fewer experts than trained with, including 55 interactive figures and runnable code.

entry.title: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber: a major advance in security research that pairs stronger capabilities with ...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused model pairing stronger offensive/defensive capabilities with improved alignment. It reportedly powered recent Linux kernel security research and is being used by security teams at Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Cisco and OpenAI itself. Access is limited to select Daybreak Red customers with expansion planned.

entry.title: GPT-6 Cyber: a major advance for security research, already being used to help defend security-criti...
entry.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman announces GPT-6 Cyber, a security-focused model reportedly used to defend security-critical software such as the Linux kernel and Firefox, with training focused on staying within operator-specified scope, plus a Daybreak Red for Critical Infrastructure program for authorized testing by approved defenders. Very high engagement (~62.5k views).

entry.title: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Small, scoring 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence I...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Thinking Machines' release of Inkling 2 Small, scoring 31 on the Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (up 18 points from Inkling Small), matching Gemini 3.8 Flash (high); planned open-weights release would make it the top open-weights model developed outside China. It launches proprietary via the Tinker platform first.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: METR estimates Anthropic is improving model capabilities at around 2× the March ...
entry.summary: Reports that METR estimates Anthropic is improving model capabilities at roughly 2x the March 2024 to October 2025 rate, possibly as high as 3x, attributing 80% of the current acceleration to AI assistance itself rather than compute scaling.

entry.title: Today, we're launching Perplexity Teammates. They are personal agents for work. And change the para...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas announces the launch of Perplexity Teammates, personal work agents that shift the paradigm from writing prompts in sessions to giving high-level goals. Rolling out to Max users on web today, with native mobile and desktop apps coming soon.

entry.title: Announcing our strategic partnership with JPMorganChase, to explore how advanced AI can support thei...
entry.summary: Greg Brockman announces an OpenAI strategic partnership with JPMorganChase focused on enterprise AI, engineering support, and especially cybersecurity applications for the financial system.

entry.title: The era of System One Vision Model is here! Introducing VFlash: parsing the visual world in parallel...
entry.summary: Jim Fan introduces VFlash, a System-1-style vision model for Physical AI that outputs fixed-length geometric predictions (bounding boxes, robot trajectories, dense 3D motion) in parallel rather than token-by-token, achieving up to 12x faster action decoding and 5.1x overall robot inference speedup on edge GPUs like Jetson Thor and DGX Spark, while also cutting 3D trajectory error by up to 61% by avoiding autoregressive error cascades.

entry.title: @wleatherman9 @Nouamanetazi @lvwerra @huggingface short answer from the handbook: at fixed total and...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf (NVIDIA) gives a technical answer on MoE design: at fixed total and active parameters, finer-grained experts help up to a point — one ablation showed loss dropping until 128 experts (each 1/4 width, top-8), with most released models using 128-384 experts and top-4 to top-8 routing; beyond that, smaller GEMMs and all-to-all communication overhead eat into step time, so the practical expert count is somewhat less sparse than loss alone suggests. Links to a handbook and Megatron flags.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 05, 2026
entry.summary:
Autonomous AI cybersecurity dominated the day. Greg Brockman announced an OpenAI agent pipeline that found, validated, and patched nearly 1,000 Linux privilege escalations — including at least 10 exploitation techniques judged novel by experts. Rare cost transparency (~$1,279 per vulnerability) drew both excitement and offense-capability concerns.

  • Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro shipped with day-0 vLLM support; Thom Wolf broke down its sparse architecture and 1M-token context
  • Anthropic used Claude to map the first 3D vault-particle structure — the batch's most-engaged AI-for-science result (429K views)
  • Artificial Analysis led benchmarking talk: cross-model cost-efficiency data, a 'Time per Task' methodology overhaul, and GLM-5.3's record em-dash usage
  • A busy M&A day: OpenAI acquired Pierre for agent-native Git hosting, Meta took conductor, Factory took humanlayer
  • Agentic AI in the wild: Perplexity's agents claimed ad wins over agencies, levelsio ported Battlefield 1942 to mobile web via Claude Code, and Runway Dev launched as a Claude Code plugin
  • Broader currents: Andrej Karpathy on why pre-2000 sci-fi missed modern AI, Nathan Lambert praising open-weight labs' delivery reliability, and 38/39 anti-data-center ballot wins signaling infrastructure-siting pushback

Overall sentiment: bullish on agentic capability milestones and open-weights momentum, with growing seriousness about autonomous security implications and AI infrastructure politics.
entry.content:
Autonomous AI cybersecurity dominated the day. Greg Brockman announced an OpenAI agent pipeline that found, validated, and patched nearly 1,000 Linux privilege escalations — including at least 10 exploitation techniques judged novel by experts. Rare cost transparency (~$1,279 per vulnerability) drew both excitement and offense-capability concerns.

  • Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro shipped with day-0 vLLM support; Thom Wolf broke down its sparse architecture and 1M-token context
  • Anthropic used Claude to map the first 3D vault-particle structure — the batch's most-engaged AI-for-science result (429K views)
  • Artificial Analysis led benchmarking talk: cross-model cost-efficiency data, a 'Time per Task' methodology overhaul, and GLM-5.3's record em-dash usage
  • A busy M&A day: OpenAI acquired Pierre for agent-native Git hosting, Meta took conductor, Factory took humanlayer
  • Agentic AI in the wild: Perplexity's agents claimed ad wins over agencies, levelsio ported Battlefield 1942 to mobile web via Claude Code, and Runway Dev launched as a Claude Code plugin
  • Broader currents: Andrej Karpathy on why pre-2000 sci-fi missed modern AI, Nathan Lambert praising open-weight labs' delivery reliability, and 38/39 anti-data-center ballot wins signaling infrastructure-siting pushback

Overall sentiment: bullish on agentic capability milestones and open-weights momentum, with growing seriousness about autonomous security implications and AI infrastructure politics.

entry.title: we've found, validated, and prepared patches for almost 1,000 linux local privilege escalations usin...
entry.summary: Greg Brockman reports that an AI-driven cyber vulnerability pipeline found, validated, and prepared patches for nearly 1,000 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities at roughly $1,000 per vulnerability, framing this as a scalable approach to hardening open source and proprietary software.

entry.title: Our security researchers built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patchi...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces its security researchers built an autonomous vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline that, in a single run with an upcoming cyber model, validated and patched 948 Linux kernel local privilege escalation vulnerabilities at about $1.2M in API cost.

entry.title: @shostekofsky There are a few notable counter-examples (e.g. HAL) but this is basically right for a ...
entry.summary: Andrej Karpathy responds to a discussion about why pre-2000 science fiction largely failed to predict modern AI (with HAL as a notable counter-example). He outlines the chain of developments that a hypothetical AI correct around the 1970s would have needed to anticipate: the digitization of knowledge work across billions of screens, the emergence of a global internet building on ideas like Licklider's 1963 Intergalactic Computer Network, the resulting compounding repository of big data capturing human reasoning and creativity, and the shift toward statistical learning rather than hand-programmed intelligence.

entry.title: We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a va...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces that its biology research team used Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life. Vault particles, large barrel-shaped protein structures discovered in 1986, have unknown function; showing similar proteins in bacteria assemble into vaults may simplify studying their role in human cells. The post frames the project as a demonstration of AI's potential and limitations in accelerating science.

entry.title:
Kimi-K3.1-Pro by Moonshot AI: interesting facts
It's huge, and sparse • It has 2.8T total parameter...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf breaks down Moonshot AI's Kimi-K3.1-Pro architecture: 2.8T total parameters with 104B active per token across 896 experts (16 per token), linear attention (KDA) in most of 93 layers with periodic DeepSeek-style sparse attention for 1M-token context, a custom SiTU-GLU activation, a 401M vision encoder, and MXFP4 4-bit training making the repo about 1.56 TB versus roughly 5.6 TB in BF16, plus benchmark comparisons against other large open models.

entry.title: The agents also discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques that, to the best of o...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports that its agents discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques judged novel by consulted experts, suggesting frontier LLMs can find new exploitation approaches beyond applying known techniques.

entry.title: A $100 budget buys 40 Intelligence Index tasks (a mix of task archetypes) with Opus 5.5 at medium re...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis quantifies cost-efficiency across frontier models: $100 buys 40 Intelligence Index tasks with Claude Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, 10 at max effort, versus 166 tasks with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and 2,500 with GPT-6 Luna at medium effort.

entry.title:
🎉 Kimi K3.1 Pro from @Kimi_Moonshot lands in vLLM on day 0!
A 1M-token context window for long codi...
entry.summary: vLLM announces Day-0 support for Moonshot's newly released open-weights Kimi K3.1 Pro, featuring a 1M-token context window for long coding sessions and 3D creation, scoring 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with the Claude Code harness, with serving across GPUs and TPUs plus RL support.

entry.summary: Ben Tossell flags an unusually busy acquisition day in AI: humanlayer acquired by Factory, conductor by Meta, and pierre by OpenAI.

entry.title: The run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities. It produced proofs of concept for 291 information leaks an...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports the run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, produced PoCs for 291 information leaks and working exploits for 948 distinct Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities that succeeded on stock desktop configurations with standard protections.

entry.title: Announcing the next version of Artificial Analysis API Performance Benchmarking: Time per Task is no...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a major update to its API performance benchmarking across ~1,000 serverless endpoints: Time per Task becomes the headline metric (output tokens per task divided by end-to-end output speed), and End-to-End Output Speed now measures from request send to final token, including prefill and hidden-reasoning waits, reflecting agentic workloads where total task time matters more than per-token speed.

entry.title: The full run cost $1,213,430 in API credits—about $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vul...
entry.summary: OpenAI discloses the run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, roughly $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vulnerability, and compares against historical Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN bounty values of $18.9M-$66.3M to argue AI makes defensive analysis cost-effective.

entry.title: In AA-PersonalityBench, GLM-5.3 uses the most em dashes of any model measured, averaging 7.4 per res...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's AA-PersonalityBench finds GLM-5.3 uses the most em dashes of any measured model (7.4 per response), while Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 use almost none; Claude Fable 5.1 averages 6.4 and rankings list highest and lowest stylometric outliers.

entry.title: Cognition's new flash model is post-trained on top of Inkling-small!
entry.summary: Soumith Chintala highlights that Cognition's new flash model is post-trained on top of Inkling-small, a notable detail about the lineage of the coding-agent company's model.

entry.title:
There is a false equivalence being made between open source software and AI benchmarks.
The argum...
entry.summary: Husain's anchor post arguing that criticizing AI benchmarks differs from the OSS norm of fixing instead of complaining: benchmark results are consumed at face value for decisions, used like a credit score or Yelp rating, come with no disclaimers, and are brittle in ways consumers cannot verify without trace-analysis skills. He calls for healthy skepticism and better communication rather than deflecting criticism.

entry.title: Very interesting how the open model labs in China always have delivered on their promises of when we...
entry.summary: Lambert observes that Chinese open-weight labs have consistently delivered weights on their promised timelines, and predicts it will be telling when one inevitably fails to hit a scheduled release.

entry.title: AI semiotics: cool paper suggests that AIs are strongly impacted by visual symbols in ways they do n...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick highlights a research paper suggesting AI models are strongly influenced by visual symbols in ways not reflected in their own chains of thought, and that their interpretation of such symbols differs markedly from human readings.

entry.title: > we developed and trained Ripple-65B Preview for only $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the prev...
entry.summary: swyx quotes a claim that Ripple-65B Preview was trained for $32M in total R&D cost (including pretraining ladder, data mixing, evals, synthetic data, and posttraining), one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA on agentic coding, calling it the Avengers of open model SOTA.

entry.title:
K3.1 combines DSA sparse attention with recurrent Kimi Delta Attention.
One packed cache holds MLA ...
entry.summary: Technical breakdown of Kimi K3.1's architecture combining DSA sparse attention with recurrent Kimi Delta Attention, using a single packed cache for MLA latents, indexer keys and KDA state, plus serving optimizations like token-sharded prefill and fused low-latency decode.

Opponents are also ahead in all six races with partial counts, while one Maine town has yet to report. This signals strong grassroots resistance to AI data center infrastructure buildout.

entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports that leading labs ship API defaults below max effort, sharply reducing Time per Task: GPT-6 Astra scores 52 at medium effort vs 57 at max (~5.8 vs ~18 min), GPT-6.1 Sol drops 55 to 46 (~3.9 vs 20.0 min), and Claude Opus 5.5 falls 59 to 48 (~6.8 vs 26.0 min). All are established models per GA dates, so this is measurement analysis rather than launch news.

entry.title: Modern multimodal AI systems struggle significantly when interpreting structured images such as char...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov shares an article introducing PixelCraft, a multi-agent framework aimed at improving multimodal AI interpretation of structured visuals like charts, plots, and geometric diagrams. It argues that small perceptual errors on axes or bars cause cascading reasoning failures, and that prior approaches (text-only chain-of-thought or rigid one-way image edits) lack fidelity and flexibility. PixelCraft combines image-grounding tools with high-fidelity editing and non-linear reasoning so models can revisit assumptions and explore alternate interpretations.
